title: sync --to-disk refuses beside a daemon watching the tree, though it runs no ingest and lands only a projection
body:
**Seen.** At 16:08Z on 2026-09-21, vc ran `intent sync --to-disk` in the Intent checkout while intentd was watching this tree, and it refused. The refusal gave the two-families reason: "`sync` and `ingest` are the two families that would genuinely run twice against it". Its remedy was "stop the daemon process and run again".

**Expected.** A store-to-disk projection runs beside the daemon, as every mutating verb's projection did all that afternoon (`wb add`, `wb archive`, `issues close`). Such a projection lands only the bytes that differ and records them as landed, so the daemon does not read them back as an edit.

**Why this looks wrong, from a source READ, not a drive.** Nobody has yet run `--to-disk` beside a live daemon to show that it is harmless.

- The refusal is in the CLI's one store door, not the library. `engine()` at `intent-cli/src/render.rs:604` refuses a `StoreNeed::Exclusive` open when `watching_this_project` answers yes.
- Only two call sites open `Exclusive`: `sync --to-disk` at `render.rs:1237` and `sync --to-store` at `render.rs:1247`. `sync --apply` opens `Shared`, and the guide calls it safe beside a running daemon.
- `Facade::sync_to_disk` at `intentsvcs/src/facade.rs:8159` has no daemon check of its own. It loads canon from the store, projects the views, commits only the paths whose bytes differ, and records what landed. It runs no ingest walk and watches nothing.
- The hazard the refusal names, two engines both ingesting one tree, is real for `--to-store`, which replaces the store from the extract and so races the daemon's ingest. The read finds no such hazard for `--to-disk`.

**Candidate fix, as a candidate.** Open `sync --to-disk` as `Shared` and keep `sync --to-store` `Exclusive`. Add a test that drives `--to-disk` beside a daemon watching the tree and checks that the daemon does not re-ingest what landed.

**One line in the same place.** The `Exclusive` doc comment at `render.rs:168` still says the predicate "fires on any answering daemon, not on one watching THIS project". The code already narrows to this project, so the comment is stale.

**What this does NOT block.** This refusal blocks nothing that was waiting on it. The seven closed-issue views still carrying the 3.1.0 footer were never waiting on `sync --to-disk`. cc measured, and vc confirmed, that a closed issue's view leaves the disk through `intent organize --apply`, which today's closes skipped. So the refresh path was never the door for them. The refusal has a remedy, which is to stop the daemon and run again, hence severity low.


**As landed** (ic, 2026-09-21, landing 895afda76, patch-id eaa6388eacaf7e0b91a3a77b8351c1d25047ad7e, identical to the bank vc judged from refs/bank/ic/0500/985d440b7).

**The change.** `sync --to-disk` opens the store through the shared door. `sync --to-store` is now the one `Exclusive` site, and its refusal beside a watching daemon names it: it replaces the store from the extract, which would race the daemon's own ingest of the same tree. The `Exclusive` doc no longer carries the stale sentence about the predicate firing on any answering daemon, and it says why each direction is where it is. `intent/docs/releasing.md` step 0 stays. Its ground moved: it named this refusal, and it now names the release driver's own pre-flight and `build all` swapping the binary a running daemon was started from.

**CORRECTED FORWARD: THE MECHANISM THIS BODY GAVE IS WRONG.** The body above credits `record_landed` with keeping the daemon off what `--to-disk` lands. The measurement says the watcher's SCOPE does:
- removing a generated view from a watched tree costs the daemon no ingest, and the view stays gone;
- the new arm stays green with the `record_landed` call deleted from `sync_to_disk`, compiled and confirmed.

The verb was right to run beside the daemon, and the reason given for it was not. `record_landed` stays, for what other tests own. The new arm guards the scope: it goes red if the watcher ever takes in the views a landing writes, which is the loop issue 0311 was about.

**The arm.** `sync_to_disk_runs_beside_a_watching_daemon.rs` runs beside a real watching daemon:
1. It asserts the daemon is watching, as anti-vacuity.
2. It measures what a sentinel thread file costs from rest to rest, as the control.
3. It removes an issue view while the tree is watched, and asserts the removal cost 0.
4. `sync --to-disk` must succeed and put the view back.
5. A second sentinel's cost must equal the control's, and the landed bytes must be unchanged after it.

It uses an issue view and removes it while watched because a thread ingest re-renders every view, and so does the first ingest after registration. Its presence waits are counted in tries, never on a clock.

**Controls.**
- With the old `open_exclusive()` restored at the `--to-disk` site, the arm goes red with the refusal text.
- With `record_landed` removed, it stays green, as described above.

**The six arms** that proved the refusal with `--to-disk` now prove it with `--to-store`, each with its control on the same verb. The sixth, in `sync_plan_and_apply_from_the_command_line.rs`, was missed by the plan and found red by the first whole run. It is renamed `apply_runs_where_a_daemon_watches_and_to_store_refuses`.

**The judging run** used a private worktree, an in-tree target dir and a fresh HOME:
- fmt was clean, and clippy with `-D warnings` gave 0 warnings.
- intentsvcs passed 299 and 1525, with 4 ignored.
- intent-cli passed 321 and 724, at load 369 before and 436 after.
- The new arm's absence half was judged at the floor: green at load 11.09 before and 10.60 after.

**Routed and landed.** The release driver's pre-flight text at `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release:645-661` gave this refusal as its reason. The check stands on the binary swap, so only the text was wrong. It was dc's, and dc corrected both texts to the binary-swap ground at c7363add8, leaving the check alone.

**Driven on the shipped pair** (ic, 17:48Z). `intent --version` and the running intentd both reported 850918a73, after hv's restart; `intent daemon status` read "running intentd 3.2.0 (850918a73...), the commit the intentd beside this intent names". In the Intent checkout, on a pristine tree beside that live, watching daemon, `intent sync --to-disk` answered `ok: extract written for 78 thread(s); prose, shipped content and wip/restart are not modelled and are unchanged` at rc 0. `git status` was empty before and after, so it wrote nothing that differed. On 3.2.0 the same command refused here at 16:08Z.
